title.en: The Big Bang & the Expanding Universe

clips.send: Protons and neutrons form. After about 10 millionths of a second it is “cool” enough (a few trillion degrees) for quarks to clump in threes into protons and neutrons.
clips.text: Protons and neutrons form. After about 10 millionths of a second it is “cool” enough (a few trillion degrees) for quarks to clump in threes into protons and neutrons.

clips.send: Quark soup. The universe is a blazing soup of quarks, electrons, light and other particles. Matter only just beats antimatter: about one extra particle for every billion pairs. That tiny leftover became everything that exists, including you.
clips.text: Quark soup. The universe is a blazing soup of quarks, electrons, light and other particles. Matter only just beats antimatter: about one extra particle for every billion pairs. That tiny leftover became everything that exists, including you.

clips.send: Life on Earth. At least 3.5 billion years ago (maybe earlier), simple single-celled microbes live in Earth’s oceans. Animals come much later: the first dinosaurs only 230 million years ago.
clips.text: Life on Earth. At least 3.5 billion years ago (maybe earlier), simple single-celled microbes live in Earth’s oceans. Animals come much later: the first dinosaurs only 230 million years ago.

clips.send: Common mix-up: Dark matter and dark energy are different things. Dark matter has gravity and holds galaxies together; dark energy makes the expansion speed up. We can measure what they do, but nobody yet knows what they are.
clips.text: Common mix-up: Dark matter and dark energy are different things. Dark matter has gravity and holds galaxies together; dark energy makes the expansion speed up. We can measure what they do, but nobody yet knows what they are.

clips.send: Galaxy GN-z11. Found by Hubble (2016), studied by Webb. We see it as it was about 400 million years after the Big Bang. Its light set out almost 9 billion years before the Sun and Earth formed.
clips.text: Galaxy GN-z11. Found by Hubble (2016), studied by Webb. We see it as it was about 400 million years after the Big Bang.. Its light set out almost 9 billion years before the Sun and Earth formed.

clips.send: The first nuclei (3–20 minutes). For about 20 minutes the whole universe is a nuclear fusion reactor. Protons and neutrons fuse into helium nuclei, plus a little deuterium and lithium. Result: about 75 percent hydrogen and 25 percent helium by mass, exactly what we measure in the oldest gas and stars.

clips.send: The Sun. 150 million km away. Sunlight takes 8 minutes 20 seconds to reach Earth. If the Sun suddenly vanished, we would keep seeing it (and orbiting it) for over 8 minutes.
clips.text: The Sun. 150 million km away. Sunlight takes 8 minutes 20 seconds to reach Earth.. If the Sun suddenly vanished, we would keep seeing it (and orbiting it) for over 8 minutes.

clips.send: Dark energy takes over. As galaxies spread apart, matter’s gravity weakens and dark energy wins. The expansion, which had been slowing down, starts to speed up. Astronomers discovered this in 1998 using Type Ia supernovae.
clips.text: Dark energy takes over. As galaxies spread apart, matter’s gravity weakens and dark energy wins. The expansion, which had been slowing down, starts to speed up. Astronomers discovered this in 1998 using Type Ia supernovae.

clips.send: First atoms: the CMB is released (380,000 years). Until now light kept bouncing off free electrons, like headlights in fog. At about 3,000 K electrons join nuclei to make the first atoms, the fog clears, and light travels freely. That light is the cosmic microwave background we still detect today.

clips.send: Cosmic noon. About 3 billion years in, galaxies make new stars roughly 10 times faster than today. Galaxies collide and merge, and giant black holes in their centers blaze as quasars.
clips.text: Cosmic noon. About 3 billion years in, galaxies make new stars roughly 10 times faster than today. Galaxies collide and merge, and giant black holes in their centers blaze as quasars.

clips.send: The first galaxies. The James Webb Space Telescope has found galaxies seen just 290 million years after the Big Bang, such as JADES-GS-z14-0, already surprisingly bright. Small galaxies merge to build bigger ones.
clips.text: The first galaxies. The James Webb Space Telescope has found galaxies seen just 290 million years after the Big Bang, such as JADES-GS-z14-0, already surprisingly bright. Small galaxies merge to build bigger ones.

clips.send: M87 in the Virgo Cluster. A giant elliptical galaxy, 53 million light-years away. Its light left about 12 million years after an asteroid wiped out the dinosaurs. Its central black hole was the first one ever photographed (2019).
clips.text: M87 in the Virgo Cluster. A giant elliptical galaxy, 53 million light-years away. Its light left about 12 million years after an asteroid wiped out the dinosaurs.. Its central black hole was the first one ever photographed (2019).

clips.send: Common mix-up: For very distant galaxies, “how long the light traveled” and “how far away it is now” are different: space kept stretching while the light was on its way.
clips.text: Common mix-up: For very distant galaxies, “how long the light traveled” and “how far away it is now” are different: space kept stretching while the light was on its way.

clips.send: Common mix-up: A light-year is a distance, not a time. But because light needs one year to cross one light-year, distance and look-back time go together, at least nearby.
clips.text: Common mix-up: A light-year is a distance, not a time. But because light needs one year to cross one light-year, distance and look-back time go together, at least nearby.

clips.send: The cosmic microwave background. The farthest light there is. Released 380,000 years after the Big Bang, from every direction at once. Before this the universe was an opaque fog: no light from earlier can reach us.
clips.text: The cosmic microwave background. The farthest light there is. Released 380,000 years after the Big Bang, from every direction at once.. Before this the universe was an opaque fog: no light from earlier can reach us.

clips.send: Galaxy JADES-GS-z14-0. Found by JWST in 2024; the distance record holder until 2025. We see it only about 290 million years after the Big Bang. Its light was stretched so much that it arrives as infrared, which is why Webb was built to see infrared.

clips.send: Cosmic dawn: the first stars. Around 100–200 million years, gas in dark-matter clumps collapses into the first stars: huge, hot and blue, made only of hydrogen and helium. When they explode they make the first carbon, oxygen and iron, and their light starts to clear the hydrogen fog (reionization).

When they explode they make the first carbon, oxygen and iron, and their light starts to clear the hydrogen fog (reionization).

clips.send: Today: 13.8 billion years. Space between the galaxies is just 2.7 degrees above absolute zero, and the expansion is speeding up. If all of cosmic history were squeezed into one year, modern humans would appear in the last 11 minutes of December 31.
clips.text: Today: 13.8 billion years. Space between the galaxies is just 2.7 degrees above absolute zero, and the expansion is speeding up. If all of cosmic history were squeezed into one year, modern humans would appear in the last 11 minutes of December 31.

clips.send: The cosmic dark ages. No stars yet: just cooling hydrogen and helium gas, and invisible dark matter slowly pulling into clumps. The leftover glow fades from orange-red into infrared, so the universe goes dark.
clips.text: The cosmic dark ages. No stars yet: just cooling hydrogen and helium gas, and invisible dark matter slowly pulling into clumps. The leftover glow fades from orange-red into infrared, so the universe goes dark.

clips.send: Inflation. In far less than a trillionth of a trillionth of a second, a tiny patch of space balloons by an enormous factor (at least 10 to the power of 26 times). Tiny quantum jitters get stretched into the seeds of every future galaxy. This is the least certain part of the story: strong clues, not yet proven.
clips.text: Inflation. In far less than a trillionth of a trillionth of a second, a tiny patch of space balloons by an enormous factor (at least 10²⁶ times). Tiny quantum jitters get stretched into the seeds of every future galaxy. This is the least certain part of the story: strong clues, not yet proven.

clips.send: Quasar 3C 273. The first quasar identified (1963). A galaxy whose central black hole is swallowing gas so fast that it outshines its whole galaxy hundreds of times over. When its light set out, life on Earth was still only single-celled.

clips.send: Center of the Milky Way. About 26,000 light-years away. Its light left during the last ice age, when mammoths roamed North America. We can’t see it with our eyes (dust blocks it), but infrared and radio telescopes can.

clips.send: Proxima Centauri. The nearest star, 4.24 light-years away. The light you would see tonight left it about 4 years ago. A message sent there by radio today would arrive around 2031, and a reply would come back around 2035.
clips.text: Proxima Centauri. The nearest star, 4.24 light-years away. The light you would see tonight left it about 4 years ago.. A message sent there by radio today would arrive around 2031, and a reply would come back around 2035.

clips.send: The Moon. 384,000 km away. Moonlight (really reflected sunlight) takes 1.3 seconds to reach you. So the Moon you see is the Moon of about one heartbeat ago.
clips.text: The Moon. 384,000 km away. Moonlight (really reflected sunlight) takes 1.3 seconds to reach you.. So the Moon you see is the Moon of about one heartbeat ago.

clips.send: The Sun and Earth form. 4.6 billion years ago, a cloud of gas enriched by generations of earlier stars collapses into the Sun and a disk that becomes the planets. The iron in your blood and the calcium in your bones were made inside those earlier stars.
clips.text: The Sun and Earth form. 4.6 billion years ago, a cloud of gas enriched by generations of earlier stars collapses into the Sun and a disk that becomes the planets. The iron in your blood and the calcium in your bones were made inside those earlier stars.

clips.send: Andromeda Galaxy. The farthest thing you can see with your eyes alone. 2.5 million light-years away: the light entering your eye left when the first members of our human genus, Homo, were appearing in Africa. On a dark autumn night you can see it as a faint smudge in the constellation Andromeda.

clips.send: 星系 GN-z11。哈勃发现（2016 年），韦布深入研究。我们看到的是它在大爆炸后约 4 亿年时的样子。它的光出发时，距离太阳和地球形成还有将近 90 亿年。

clips.send: 最早的原子核（3–20 分钟）。大约 20 分钟里，整个宇宙就是一个核聚变反应堆。质子和中子聚变成氦原子核，还有少量氘和锂。结果是：按质量算约 百分之75 的氢和 百分之25 的氦，和我们在最古老的气体和恒星里测到的完全一致。
clips.text: 最早的原子核（3–20 分钟）. 大约 20 分钟里，整个宇宙就是一个核聚变反应堆。质子和中子聚变成氦原子核，还有少量氘和锂。结果是：按质量算约 75% 的氢和 25% 的氦，和我们在最古老的气体和恒星里测到的完全一致。

clips.send: 质子和中子形成。大约十万分之一秒后，温度“降”到几万亿度，夸克三个一组结合成质子和中子。
clips.text: 质子和中子形成. 大约十万分之一秒后，温度“降”到几万亿度，夸克三个一组结合成质子和中子。

clips.send: 太阳和地球形成。46 亿年前，一团被前几代恒星“加料”的气体云坍缩成了太阳，以及后来形成行星的圆盘。你血液里的铁和骨头里的钙，都是在那些更早的恒星里造出来的。
clips.text: 太阳和地球形成. 46 亿年前，一团被前几代恒星“加料”的气体云坍缩成了太阳，以及后来形成行星的圆盘。你血液里的铁和骨头里的钙，都是在那些更早的恒星里造出来的。

clips.send: 容易混淆：暗物质和暗能量不是一回事。暗物质有引力，把星系“拉”在一起；暗能量让宇宙膨胀越来越快。我们只知道它们的效果，还不知道它们到底是什么。

clips.send: 地球上出现生命。至少 35 亿年前（也许更早），简单的单细胞微生物生活在地球的海洋里。动物出现得晚得多：最早的恐龙只在 2.3 亿年前。

clips.send: 最早的原子：宇宙微波背景辐射释放（38 万年）。在此之前，光不断被自由电子弹来弹去，就像车灯照进浓雾。温度降到约 3000 K 时，电子和原子核结合成最早的原子，“雾”散了，光可以自由穿行。这些光就是我们今天还能探测到的宇宙微波背景辐射。

clips.send: 宇宙黎明：第一代恒星。大约 1 亿到 2 亿年时，暗物质团块里的气体坍缩成第一代恒星：巨大、炽热、蓝色，只含氢和氦。它们爆炸时造出了最早的碳、氧和铁，它们的光开始把氢气“雾”电离、驱散（再电离）。
clips.text: 宇宙黎明：第一代恒星. 大约 1 亿到 2 亿年时，暗物质团块里的气体坍缩成第一代恒星：巨大、炽热、蓝色，只含氢和氦。它们爆炸时造出了最早的碳、氧和铁，它们的光开始把氢气“雾”电离、驱散（再电离）。

clips.send: 夸克汤。宇宙是一锅炽热的“汤”：夸克、电子、光和其他粒子。物质只比反物质多了一点点：每十亿对粒子里大约多出一个。这一点点剩余，后来变成了存在的一切，包括你。

clips.send: 类星体 3C 273。第一个被确认的类星体（1963 年）。这个星系中心的黑洞吞噬气体的速度极快，发出的光比整个星系亮几百倍。它的光出发时，地球上的生命还只有单细胞生物。
clips.text: 类星体 3C 273. 第一个被确认的类星体（1963 年）. 这个星系中心的黑洞吞噬气体的速度极快，发出的光比整个星系亮几百倍。. 它的光出发时，地球上的生命还只有单细胞生物。

clips.send: 室女座星系团中的 M87。巨型椭圆星系，5300 万光年。它的光出发时，小行星灭绝恐龙才过去约 1200 万年。它中心的黑洞是人类拍到的第一个黑洞（2019 年）。
clips.text: 室女座星系团中的 M87. 巨型椭圆星系，5300 万光年. 它的光出发时，小行星灭绝恐龙才过去约 1200 万年。. 它中心的黑洞是人类拍到的第一个黑洞（2019 年）。

clips.send: 月球。距离 38.4 万千米。月光（其实是反射的太阳光）到达你眼睛需要 1.3 秒。所以你看到的，是大约一次心跳之前的月亮。

clips.send: 暗能量占上风。随着星系越离越远，物质的引力减弱，暗能量占了上风。原本在减速的膨胀开始加速。1998 年天文学家用 Ia 型超新星发现了这一点。

clips.send: 今天：138 亿年。星系之间的空间只比绝对零度高 2.7 度，宇宙膨胀还在加速。如果把整个宇宙历史压缩成一年，现代人类要到 12 月 31 日的最后 11 分钟才出现。

clips.send: 星系 JADES-GS-z14-0。韦布望远镜 2024 年发现，2025 年以前的最远纪录保持者。我们看到的是它在大爆炸后仅约 2.9 亿年时的样子。它的光被拉长得太厉害，到达时已经是红外线，这正是韦布望远镜要看红外线的原因。

clips.send: 宇宙黑暗时代。还没有恒星，只有逐渐冷却的氢气和氦气，以及看不见的暗物质在引力作用下慢慢聚成团。残留的光从橙红色褪成红外线，宇宙变得一片黑暗。
clips.text: 宇宙黑暗时代. 还没有恒星，只有逐渐冷却的氢气和氦气，以及看不见的暗物质在引力作用下慢慢聚成团。残留的光从橙红色褪成红外线，宇宙变得一片黑暗。

clips.send: 宇宙正午。大约 30 亿年时，星系形成新恒星的速度约为今天的 10 倍。星系不断碰撞、合并，中心的巨型黑洞以类星体的形式发出耀眼的光。

clips.send: 银河系中心。约 2.6 万光年。它的光出发时，地球正处于上一个冰期，猛犸象还在北美洲漫步。我们用肉眼看不到它（被尘埃挡住了），但红外和射电望远镜可以。

clips.send: 容易混淆：光年是距离单位，不是时间单位。但因为光走 1 光年正好要 1 年，所以（至少在近处）距离和回溯时间是对应的。

clips.send: 最早的星系。詹姆斯·韦布空间望远镜发现了大爆炸后仅 2.9 亿年的星系，比如 JADES-GS-z14-0，它们已经亮得出人意料。小星系不断合并成更大的星系。

clips.send: 容易混淆：对于非常遥远的星系，“光走了多久”和“它现在有多远”是两回事：光在路上的时候，空间一直在拉伸。

clips.send: 比邻星。最近的恒星，4.24 光年。你今晚看到的光，大约 4 年前就从它那里出发了。今天用无线电发一条消息过去，约 2031 年才到；回信要到约 2035 年才能收到。

clips.send: 仙女星系。你用肉眼能看到的最远天体。250 万光年外：进入你眼睛的光出发时，人属的最早成员才刚刚在非洲出现。秋天无光污染的夜晚，你可以在仙女座看到它：一小片朦胧的光斑。

clips.send: 暴胀。在远远不到一万亿分之一的一万亿分之一秒里，一小块空间急剧膨胀了极其巨大的倍数（至少 10的26次方 倍）。微小的量子涨落被拉大，成了后来所有星系的“种子”。这是整个故事里最不确定的部分：有有力的线索，但还没被证实。

clips.send: 宇宙微波背景辐射。能看到的最远的光。在大爆炸后 38 万年释放，来自四面八方。在那之前，宇宙是一团不透明的“雾”：更早的光无法到达我们这里。

clips.send: 太阳。距离 1.5 亿千米。阳光到达地球需要 8 分 20 秒。如果太阳突然消失，我们还会继续看到它（并继续绕它转）8 分多钟。
